'''Viqar Uddin Ahmad''' (6 July 1940 – 29 June 2019) was a Pakistani [[organic chemistry|organic chemist]] who specialised in the [[natural product chemistry|chemistry of natural products]] at the H. E. J. Research Institute of Chemistry, [[University of Karachi]].<ref name=News2019>{{cite news |title=Senior scientist Prof Dr Viqar Uddin Ahmed passes away |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/497933-senior-scientist-prof-dr-viqar-uddin-ahmed-passes-away |work=thenews.com.pk |publisher=The News International |date=30 June 2019 |access-date=20 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=SpringerSDSG>{{cite book |last1=Ahmad |first1=Viqar Uddin |last2=Basha |first2=Anwer |title=Spectroscopic Data of Steroid Glycosides: Volume 1 |publisher=Springer |location=New York |year=2006 |isbn=978-0-387-31161-6 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-39571-5}}</ref> He served as co-director from 1990 to 1999 and as dean of the university's Faculty of Science from 1994 to 2000.<ref name=News2019/>

==Early life and education==
Ahmad was born on 6 July 1940 in [[Allahabad]], [[British India]].<ref name=News2019/> He completed his MSc in chemistry at the [[University of Allahabad]] in 1959, standing first in his class and receiving a gold medal from the university.<ref name=News2019/> After moving to Pakistan, he enrolled as a doctoral student at the [[University of Karachi]], where he worked under the supervision of the organic chemist [[Salimuzzaman Siddiqui]] and, in 1966, became the first person to be awarded a PhD in chemistry by the university.<ref name=News2019/><ref name=HEJWelcome>{{cite web |title=H.E.J. Research Institute of Chemistry – Welcome |url=https://iccs.edu/page-research-institute-of-chemistry |access-date=20 April 2026 |website=iccs.edu |publisher=International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences |language=en}}</ref> He subsequently moved to [[West Germany]] for post-doctoral studies and was awarded a second doctorate (Dr. rer. nat.) by the [[University of Bonn]] in 1968.<ref name=News2019/><ref name=Kazakhstan>{{cite web |title=An Example of Successful Scientific Collaboration Between Pakistan and Kazakhstan |url=https://dokumen.pub/an-example-of-successful-scientific-collaboration-between-pakistan-and-kazakhstan-9786012476323.html |access-date=27 July 2026 |website=dokumen.pub |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Ahmad was associated with the H. E. J. Research Institute of Chemistry from its foundation within the University of Karachi's Department of Chemistry in 1967.<ref name=SpringerSDSG/><ref name=HEJWelcome/> He became a full professor at the institute in 1976 and was later awarded a Doctor of Science (D.Sc.) by the University of Karachi in 1992.<ref name=Kazakhstan/> From 1988 to 1989, he held an Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship at [[Erlangen]], Germany.<ref name=Kazakhstan/>

When the institute was reorganised in 1990 into the [[International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences]] (ICCBS) under the directorship of [[Atta-ur-Rahman (chemist)|Atta-ur-Rahman]], Ahmad was appointed co-director of the H. E. J. Research Institute, a position he held until his retirement from the post in 1999.<ref name=News2019/> He was appointed dean of the Faculty of Science at the University of Karachi on 19 March 1994 and held the post until his formal retirement on 5 July 2000; one week later, on 12 July 2000, he was reappointed as professor at the H. E. J. Research Institute of Chemistry, where he continued to supervise research for the remainder of his life.<ref name=News2019/>

Ahmad's research focused on the isolation, purification and structural elucidation of biologically active natural products from Pakistani medicinal plants, and on the chemistry of [[alkaloid]]s, [[terpenoid]]s, [[saponin]]s and carbohydrates.<ref name=FreeLib>{{cite news |title=Academicians condole death of Prof. Viqar Uddin Ahmed |url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Academicians+condole+death+of+Prof.+Viqar+Uddin+Ahmed-a0593401824 |work=thefreelibrary.com |publisher=Pakistan & Gulf Economist |date=14 July 2019 |access-date=20 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=SpringerSDSG/> His work on compounds includes eudesmane [[sesquiterpene]]s with activity against ''[[Escherichia coli]]'', ''[[Staphylococcus aureus]]'' and ''[[Bacillus anthracis]]'', [[triterpene|triterpenoidal]] and steroidal saponins with [[brine shrimp]] toxicity, and a saponin from a Turkish plant that showed [[hypotension|hypotensive]] activity in anaesthetised rats.<ref name=SpringerSDSG/>

During a nine-month [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellowship]] in 1993, Ahmad was a visiting researcher at [[Cornell University]] in [[Ithaca, New York]], where he contributed to the 12-step total synthesis of an alkaloid isolated from an insect. During the same fellowship, he also lectured in the chemistry departments of [[Central Michigan University]], [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]] and [[Georgia State University]].<ref name=SpringerSDSG/>

From 1995, Ahmad served as an editor of the ''[[Journal of the Chemical Society of Pakistan]]'', succeeding Z. H. Zaidi and working alongside Atta-ur-Rahman.<ref name=EVISA>{{cite web |title=Journal of the Chemical Society of Pakistan |url=https://speciation.net/Database/Journals/Journal-of-the-Chemical-Society-of-Pakistan-;i320 |access-date=20 April 2026 |website=speciation.net |publisher=EVISA |language=en}}</ref> He was an elected member of the Council of the [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] and a fellow of the academy, as well as a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences|The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS)]], formerly the Third World Academy of Sciences, and of the [[Chemical Society of Pakistan]].<ref name=News2019/>

==Selected bibliography==
Ahmad authored or co-authored eight books.<ref name=News2019/>
* Atta-ur-Rahman and V. U. Ahmad, ''13C-NMR of Natural Products'' (Springer, 1992).<ref name=SpringerCarotane>{{cite book |last1=Atta-ur-Rahman |last2=Ahmad |first2=V. U. |chapter=Carotane |title=13C-NMR of Natural Products |publisher=Springer |location=Boston, MA |year=1992 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4615-3290-3_22 |isbn=978-1-4613-6447-4}}</ref>
* V. U. Ahmad and A. Basha, ''Spectroscopic Data of Steroid Glycosides'' (five volumes, Springer, 2006–2007), covering over 3,500 naturally occurring steroid glycosides.<ref name=SpringerSDSG/>

==Awards and honours==
The [[Government of Pakistan]] conferred the [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz]] on him on 23 March 1996, and the higher civil award [[Hilal-i-Imtiaz]] on 23 March 2006.<ref name=News2019/> On 4 February 1998, he received the [[Khwarizmi International Award|Khwarizmi Prize]] from the [[President of Iran]] at a ceremony in [[Tehran]].<ref name=News2019/> He was awarded the DuPont Science Cash Award in Chemistry in 2003 and, in March 2004, was appointed a Distinguished National Professor by the [[Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)|Higher Education Commission]] of Pakistan. He received the commission's Outstanding Research Award for 2005–06.<ref name=News2019/>
